# 1.2.61 - tests that say what they measured

The fifth stage on the way to 1.3.0. Almost all of it is for the people who
build and check the module rather than for the table: the tests are split into
files by what they may touch, every test has to show that it measured
something, and every change to the module is now run on GitHub before it can
be released. Three things change for a GM, listed first. Nothing here asks a
world to be migrated.

## Changed

- **`game.drpg.runTests()` runs tier 1 unless you ask for more.** Tier 2
  writes to the world, so `runTests({ tier: 2 })` opens a window that names the
  world and waits for you to confirm; Cancel is the default. The result line
  gains a fourth number when some tests are known to stay red until a later
  stage: "N passed, N failed, N skipped, K red until a later stage".
- **An Assistant GM is now checked like a player** when Daggerheart asks the
  GM's browser to make a change for them.
- **`game.drpg.migrateRemnants()` now removes what it said it removed.** The
  step that took the answer key off an old trace token used a form of update
  this Foundry ignores, so it removed nothing. It now moves what the token
  holds into the GMs' record of traces, reads the record back, and only then
  removes it from the token. A trace the GM promoted at a body discovery keeps
  that promotion. The summary at the end lists every promotion it carried and
  every trace it left as it was or could not finish.
- For contributors: `npm test` in `audit/harness` runs lint, the repository
  checks, the release gate's self-test, the headless suite and every scenario
  in one go. GitHub runs the same on each push and pull request, and the
  release workflow refuses a version whose checks are red. CONTRIBUTING.md
  and CLAUDE.md say how.

## Checked

- The headless suite: 304 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped, 0 red until a later
  stage. The fourteen scenarios the continuous integration runs all end green;
  the known leaks two of them and the secrets canary measure are marked with
  the stage that closes them. New in the suite: R151 to R160. `npm test` took
  8 minutes 28 seconds here.
- The harness behaves more like Foundry v14 where the module depends on it:
  update operators, the Assistant role, Daggerheart's roll pipeline and its
  requests to the GM's browser, update hooks that edit the update, and the
  module's six stylesheets attached as v14 attaches them.
- An independent review of the stage in three parts (the harness and tools,
  security, whether the tests really measure) found no blocker, three larger
  problems and 34 smaller ones. The three larger ones are fixed here: a check
  that would not have noticed a login written in Playwright's usual form,
  three world scans that passed on a world with nothing to scan, and the trace
  migration dropping a promotion the GM had made. Of the smaller ones, one
  moves to 1.2.63 (how the trace migration behaves when several GMs keep their
  own records), and the rest of two test clean-ups to later stages; every
  other one is fixed, and each fix was shown failing on the fault it names
  before it passed.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet, and listed in the audit's live checks
  (LIVE-E30-01 to 10): what v14 does with the old way of deleting a key and
  with the update operators, what an update hook receives, what an Assistant
  may do, what happens when someone leaves, the trace migration on a copy of
  an old world, the installed versions of the other modules, how v14 attaches
  the module's stylesheets, and the tier-2 window as v14 draws it. The local
  release gate (the live suite, the sandbox scenarios and the migration drill)
  needs a local Foundry v14 and did not run for this release.
